TECHNOLOGY_DECISIONS.PURPOSE: Defines the transport, cryptographic format, server-side token storage, Android distribution, and endpoint-security technologies for the opaque realtime wake-event flow specified by RA36-001.
TECHNOLOGY_DECISIONS.DECISION: Use self-hosted ntfy Server v2.34.0 as the sole realtime push server and ntfy Android v1.25.2 as the UnifiedPush distributor. The BFE Chat Android application integrates connector 3.3.5, receives the push in its own process, and creates the Android system notification.

Use the UnifiedPush registration endpoint with its p256dh public key and auth secret as the Web Push subscription. Encrypt payloads using RFC 8291 and the aes128gcm content encoding. The selected Go standard-library primitives are P-256 ECDH, HKDF-SHA256, and AES-GCM.

The encrypted application payload contains only protocol version and opaque wakeToken. Use generic notification text; keep wakeToken in the notification's internal navigation state, not in visible notification text or a URL.

Generate wakeToken with Go crypto/rand and persist its conversation mapping in PostgreSQL. Resolve tokens only through the protected Chat API; authorization and token-lifecycle behavior follow REQ36-WAKE-TOKEN and REQ32-AUTH.

Store the UnifiedPush endpoint, public encryption key, and authentication secret as protected subscription data associated with the authenticated BFE account. Registration, replacement, and removal use the protected Chat API and session-bound DPoP. A subscription identifies a delivery destination and grants no conversation or history access. Registration secrets, endpoint URLs, wakeToken values, and full push payloads are not logged or returned to other accounts.

Treat the registered push endpoint as a bearer capability. Require HTTPS and require its origin to match the configured ntfy server origin. Reject arbitrary client-supplied hosts, redirects, invalid schemes, and origins outside the configured ntfy server to prevent server-side request forgery. The endpoint value cannot expand the configured destination origin.

Run ntfy v2.34.0 as a private self-hosted HTTPS instance with auth-default-access: deny-all. Follow the documented ntfy UnifiedPush distributor setup: the BFE Chat publisher uses anonymous write-only access to the up* topic pattern and has no ntfy account/admin credentials; the ntfy Android distributor uses a regular non-admin account with read-only access to the up* topic pattern. Never grant anonymous read or read-write access, and never grant anonymous access to all topics. Use the endpoint and topic returned by the ntfy UnifiedPush registration. Encrypt each payload according to RFC 8291 for its registered endpoint; ntfy topic access does not replace Chat API authorization. Do not expose ntfy administrative credentials to BFE Chat or end-user clients.

The BFE Chat Android client posts a generic system notification. Its internal intent carries protocol version and wakeToken. Activation resolves the token through the protected Chat API before conversation navigation and authenticated history retrieval.

When Chat is administratively disabled, new Chat operations, history requests, wakeToken resolution, and new UnifiedPush registrations are denied. An already-active ntfy subscription may continue delivering only the opaque wake payload; receiving it does not authorize any API request. After re-enable, authorized clients catch up through the existing history API.

Commit the message before attempting ntfy delivery. A delivery failure never rolls back a persisted message; record the failure without logging secrets. An idempotent message replay must not create a new logical notification. Missed messages are recovered through authenticated history. The retry or queue mechanism is a technology implementation detail as long as these behaviors are preserved.

PostgreSQL 18.4 stores conversation data, authoritative message history, read state, and durable wakeToken mappings. pgx v5 provides PostgreSQL access and transaction support; Goose v3 manages schema migrations. BFE Drive Internal Auth over UDS validates session-bound DPoP. Realtime events are hints only; persisted conversation history remains authoritative for catch-up, ordering, visibility, and read state. No API versioning, legacy-data migration, or legacy-client support is introduced by these technology choices.
TECHNOLOGY_DECISIONS.COMPATIBILITY_CHECK: Runtime interoperability among ntfy Server v2.34.0, ntfy Android distributor v1.25.2, and Android UnifiedPush connector 3.3.5 has not yet been verified. Validate RFC 8291 aes128gcm delivery with the selected Go standard-library primitives, the configured ntfy access policy, endpoint-origin enforcement, offline delivery, notification activation, and fail-closed wakeToken resolution against these versions.
